To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
protein‐detecting microarray technologies have the potential to revolutionize protein detection in predictive and early diagnosis.

(a) the protein–protein interaction microarray is a useful technology for studying protein–protein interactions and protein–ligand interactions; (b) the microarray technology is also useful for the development of protein‐based biomarkers for predictive/early diagnosis; (c) the technology is also useful in the discovery and development of new drugs; and (d) the technology has been used in the study of the molecular basis of disease and in the study of protein–DNA interactions.
the array technology for screening disease‐related biomarkers in predictive diagnosis is a promising approach for the early detection of diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and use of protein‐detecting microarray technology in the context of predictive/early diagnosis, and the identification and validation of biomarkers for the early diagnosis of cancer, cardiovascular disease and other diseases.

the development of array‐based techniques to identify disease‐associated biomarker candidates in serum, and to develop multiplex immunoarray assays for the detection and quantification of these biomarkers.
the application of microarray technology for the detection of protein biomarkers in predictive and early diagnosis of diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein‐based microarray technology has the potential to become a valuable tool for predictive/early diagnosis of human diseases.
protein arrays have the potential to be used as a diagnostic tool in the near future.
the future of protein microarrays in the field of predictive/early diagnosis is very promising.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

protein‐detecting microarray technology has the potential to provide the basis for a new generation of protein‐based diagnostic tests for a wide variety of human diseases, including cancers, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, infectious diseases, autoimmune diseases, and neurological disorders, as well as for the development of new therapeutic drugs and vaccines.
the development and validation of new protein‐based biomarkers is an important and promising area of research for the development of predictive/early diagnosis of diseases.
protein‐based diagnosis is a new field that is rapidly developing, with the potential to revolutionize medicine.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the array‐based technologies described in this review are useful tools for biomarker discovery, validation, and clinical testing, and they are expected to play a major role in predictive/early disease diagnosis.

the protein microarray technology can be used to screen for biomarkers in serum samples of patients with a variety of different diseases and can be used for the development of diagnostic tests for these patients.
array‐based technologies can provide an efficient and cost‐effective means for screening disease‐related biomarkers in predictive or early diagnosis.
